blocks.title: Real engineering loops, one composable package
blocks.description: 39 skill modules consolidated from mattpocock/skills — the workflows Matt Pocock uses every day to do real engineering, not vibe coding. Module names, file layout and content mirror the upstream repository exactly.

showcase.user_prompt: We just merged a risky branch. Review it since main, then turn what we discussed into tickets for the tracker.
showcase.assistant_reply: I'll run code-review since main along the Standards and Spec axes in parallel sub-agents, then push the follow-up work into tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges via to-tickets. If anything is ambiguous, I'll grill you before writing the tickets.

items.title: 1. Run the one-time setup first
items.description: In your project, run `/setup-matt-pocock-skills`. It inspects the repo, then configures the issue tracker, the five triage-role labels and where GLOSSARY.md and docs/adr/ live. Do this once; skip it and to-spec, to-tickets, triage and wayfinder have nowhere to write.

items.title: 2. Load a module either way
items.description: Type a slash command such as `/tdd` or `/code-review`, or click the skill icon next to the composer and pick one by name. Both routes are equivalent: the module name is the command.

items.title: 3. Sharpen the idea before building
items.description: With a repo at hand use `/grill-with-docs` — an interview that writes ADRs and glossary entries as it goes. Without a repo use `/grill-me`. If a question needs running code, `/handoff` into a fresh session, run `/prototype`, then `/handoff` the answer back.

items.title: 4. Turn it into a spec and tickets
items.description: For work bigger than one session: `/to-spec` synthesises the conversation into a spec on your tracker, `/to-tickets` splits it into tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges. Work that fits one session skips straight to `/implement`.

items.title: 5. Implement, review, close out
items.description: Coding is driven by `/tdd`, one red-green slice at a time. Work tickets one by one with `/implement` (`/clear` between them), or orchestrate the whole spec with `/implement-spec`. Finish with `/code-review` — a two-axis review from a fixed point — then `/pr` for the PR body.

items.title: 6. Cross sessions and long hauls
items.description: When context runs out, `/handoff` compacts the conversation. When the work outgrows one session, `/wayfinder` lays it out as a map of decision tickets to resolve one at a time. For a long-running goal, `/chief-of-staff` coordinates subagents.

blocks.content:
## Pick your entry point

If you are not sure where to begin, find your situation in this table:

| Your situation | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| Just installed it | `/setup-matt-pocock-skills` (once) |
| I have an idea and want to think it through | `/grill-with-docs` |
| This bug is hard to pin down / got slow | `/diagnosing-bugs` |
| I need an ADR or shared terminology | `/domain-modeling` |
| Discussion is done, now split the work | `/to-spec` → `/to-tickets` → `/implement` |
| I just want tests for one behaviour | `/tdd` |
| Review a branch or PR | `/code-review` |
| The work is bigger than one session | `/wayfinder` |
| Redesign a module's interface | `/codebase-design` or `/improve-codebase-architecture` |
| Hand off to the next session or agent | `/handoff` |
| No idea which module to use | `/ask-matt` (the router) |

> Modules marked `disable-model-invocation` (`ask-matt`, `setup-matt-pocock-skills`, `grill-with-docs`, `wizard` and others) only fire when you call them by name — they will not interrupt on their own.

items.title: Engineering loops
items.description: TDD, code review, bug diagnosis, prototyping, research, retrospectives, PR writing, issue triage and giant-work planning (wayfinder) — the core daily loops, each with its own module.

items.title: Specs and tickets that survive handoff
items.description: to-spec and to-tickets turn a conversation into a spec or tracer-bullet tickets on your issue tracker; implement-spec carries them into code. Setup wires the tracker in once.

items.title: Grilling built in
items.description: grilling, grill-me and grill-with-docs stress-test plans through relentless interviews — writing ADRs and glossary entries as they go instead of letting weak assumptions reach the code.

items.title: Continuity between sessions
items.description: handoff and claude-handoff compact a conversation into a document another agent picks up immediately; chief-of-staff pursues long-running goals by coordinating subagents.

items.title: Guardrails and hygiene
items.description: git-guardrails blocks destructive git commands through hooks; setup-pre-commit adds Husky with lint-staged, type checking and tests; setup-ts-deep-modules wires dependency-cruiser.

items.title: Writing for humans and agents
items.description: writing-for-agents sharpens AGENTS.md and skill files; the writing-fragments / writing-shape / writing-beats trio takes raw material to a finished article.

blocks.title: Faithful to upstream
blocks.content: All 39 modules are byte-identical to mattpocock/skills (MIT, revision 4ae2317) — including supporting docs, scripts and agent definitions. Modules marked as user-invoked upstream (grill-me, to-spec, retro and others) trigger when you ask for them by name. See NOTICE.md for attribution.

## Module map

- **Engineering (20)**: ask-matt, code-review, codebase-design, diagnosing-bugs, domain-modeling, grill-with-docs, implement-spec, implement, improve-codebase-architecture, pr, prototype, research, retro, setup-matt-pocock-skills, tdd, to-spec, to-tickets, triage, wayfinder, wizard
- **Productivity (7)**: grill-me, grilling, handoff, teach, to-questionnaire, wait-what, writing-for-agents
- **Misc (4)**: git-guardrails-claude-code, migrate-to-shoehorn, scaffold-exercises, setup-pre-commit
- **In progress (8)**: chief-of-staff, claude-handoff, loop-me, setup-ts-deep-modules, software-factory, writing-beats, writing-fragments, writing-shape

These skills are intentionally small and hackable. If one fights your repo's conventions, change it — they are designed to be adapted.
